en: to fix in place; to fasten; to secure

examples.en: I secure the ladder to the wall.
I fastened the desk leg with nails.
If you don't fix it in place, it wobbles.
I fixed the camera in place and shot it.
I'll pin this post to the top.
When the price is fixed, customers feel reassured.

explain: 움직이지 않게 붙이거나 묶을 때 써요. 값이나 위치를 바꾸지 않을 때도 써요. 저절로 그런 상태가 되면 '고정되다'예요.

phrases.en: Please fix this box in place with a string.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request form used when asking someone to fix something in place.

phrases.en: The chair is fixed to the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고정하다'와 달리 이미 움직이지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 고정하다, it describes a state that is already fixed in place.

phrases.en: The store kept the price fixed this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 값을 바꾸지 않을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing used when keeping a price unchanged rather than fastening an object.

explain_en: Use it for fastening something so it doesn't move. It also covers keeping a price or position unchanged. When it just ends up that way, use '고정되다'.

examples.en: In a cave, voices echo loudly.

examples.ko: 녹음 파일의 음질이 나빠서 말소리를 알아듣기 어려워요.
examples.en: The recording quality is bad, so it's hard to make out the speech.
The baby reacts to her mother's voice and smiles.

examples.ko: 시끄러워서 친구의 말소리도 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: It's so noisy that I can't even hear my friend's voice well.

examples.ko: 옆집 말소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of the voices from next door.
Please keep your voices down in the library.

explain: '목소리'는 그 사람만의 소리(목소리가 좋다)이고, '말소리'는 말하면서 나는 소리 자체를 가리켜요. 그래서 '말소리가 들리다', '말소리를 낮추다'처럼 들리는 소리나 크기를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 발음은 [말쏘리]예요.

phrases.en: I can hear voices from the next room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 말하는지는 몰라도 말하는 소리가 귀에 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you hear talking but may not know who is speaking.

phrases.en: It's hard to make out the voices on the radio.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들리는 말을 이해할 수 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say whether you can understand the speech you hear.

phrases.en: Your voice is so quiet that I can't hear well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 소리가 작아서 알아듣기 힘들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when speech is too quiet to understand.

explain_en: '목소리' is a person's own voice (as in '목소리가 좋다'), while '말소리' refers to the sound of speech itself. So it fits when talking about audibility or volume, as in '말소리가 들리다' and '말소리를 낮추다'. It is pronounced [말쏘리].

t90.ax: In a cave, voices echo loudly.

en: to be maintained; to remain as is

examples.ko: 이 식당은 십 년째 같은 맛이 유지돼요.
examples.en: This restaurant has kept the same taste for ten years.

examples.ko: 방 온도가 하루 종일 일정하게 유지됐어요.
examples.en: The room temperature stayed constant all day.

examples.ko: 건강이 유지되려면 매일 조금씩 운동해야 해요.
examples.en: To stay healthy, you have to exercise a little every day.

examples.ko: 올해도 이 가게의 가격은 유지될 거예요.
examples.en: This shop's prices will stay the same this year too.

examples.ko: 오래 유지되는 친구 사이에는 서로 존중이 있어요.
examples.en: Friendships that last have mutual respect.

examples.ko: 약속 시간은 그대로 유지되고 장소만 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The meeting time stays the same and only the place changed.

explain: 내가 일부러 지키면 '유지하다', 상태가 그대로 이어지면 '유지되다'예요. '관계가 유지되다', '온도가 유지되다'처럼 변화가 없는 대상 앞에서 자주 써요. 안내문이나 뉴스에서도 많이 나오는 편이에요.

phrases.en: The price stays the same this year too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그대로'와 함께 바뀌지 않는다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '그대로', it makes clear that nothing changes.

phrases.example: 두 나라의 좋은 관계가 유지되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The good relationship between the two countries is being maintained.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금도 이어지는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' means it is still continuing.

phrases.en: Your health is kept up only if you exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계속'과 함께 오래 이어진다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '계속', it adds the sense of lasting a long time.

explain_en: When you keep something on purpose, use 유지하다. When a state just continues unchanged, use 유지되다. It goes with things that stay stable, like 관계가 유지되다 or 온도가 유지되다, and it shows up often in notices and news.

dis.h: stays in the same condition over time

p.n: 보관되다 is for things stored in a place, not a condition.

examples.en: When we first meet, we say a greeting like 'Hello'.

examples.ko: 선생님이 쓰신 카드 인사말이 정말 따뜻했어요.
examples.en: The greeting in the card my teacher wrote was really warm.

examples.ko: 이 인사말은 아침에도 저녁에도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this greeting in the morning and in the evening.
Putting a name in the greeting feels friendlier.
At the wedding my father gave a short greeting speech too.
Just memorizing greetings in a foreign language makes travel fun.

explain: '인사'는 고개를 숙이거나 말로 하는 행동 전체를, 인사말은 그때 입으로 하는 말만 가리켜요. 행동은 '인사하다', 말은 '인사말을 하다'라고 해요. 윗사람에게는 '인사드리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I said a greeting at the start of the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사하는 말을 입으로 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for speaking greeting words.

phrases.en: I wrote a short greeting on the card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글로 인사를 적을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for writing a greeting.

phrases.en: I started with a short greeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사말의 길이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to describe the length of a greeting.

explain_en: '인사' covers the whole action of bowing or greeting, while 인사말 is only the words you say. The action is '인사하다' and the words are '인사말을 하다'. To someone older you say '인사드리다'.

t90.ax: Putting a name in the greeting feels friendlier.

examples.ko: 자리를 비울 때 모니터를 끄는 것이 사무실 절전의 첫걸음이에요.
examples.en: Turning off the monitor when you leave your seat is the first step to saving power in the office.

examples.ko: 한국어 공부의 첫걸음은 한글을 읽는 거예요.
examples.en: The first step in studying Korean is reading Hangul.
The baby finally took her first steps.

examples.ko: 새로운 일을 시작할 때는 첫걸음이 가장 어려워요.
examples.en: When starting something new, the first step is the hardest.

examples.ko: 이 만남이 우리 협력의 첫걸음이 되길 바라요.
examples.en: I hope this meeting becomes the first step of our cooperation.

examples.ko: 작은 습관 하나가 건강한 생활의 첫걸음이 돼요.
examples.en: One small habit becomes the first step to a healthy life.

explain: 아기의 첫 걸음처럼 실제 걸음에도 쓰고, 어떤 일의 시작이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. '첫걸음을 떼다'나 '첫걸음을 내딛다'로 자주 말하고, 비슷한 말로 '첫발'이 있어요.

phrases.en: Our baby finally took its first steps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 처음 걷는 일에 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for a baby walking for the first time.

phrases.example: 저는 오늘 새 일의 첫걸음을 내디뎠어요.
phrases.en: Today I took the first step in a new job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 일을 시작한다는 비유로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used figuratively for starting something new.
phrases.en_equiv: to set out on something new

phrases.en: Starting is hard, but it gets easier once you take the first step.
phrases.nuance_ko: '첫걸음'과 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word close in meaning to 첫걸음.

explain_en: It can mean a baby's actual first steps, but it is also widely used figuratively for the start of something. People often say '첫걸음을 떼다' or '첫걸음을 내딛다', and '첫발' is a similar word.

t90.ax: The baby finally took her first steps.

examples.en: My daughter sleeps hugging a teddy bear.
I watched a cartoon where a little bear eats honey.
I attached a little bear keychain to my bag.
A baby as cute as a little bear was born.
I bought a little outfit to put on the teddy bear.
I took a photo with the bear character at the amusement park.

explain: '곰'에 사람 이름 끝처럼 쓰는 '-돌이'를 붙여 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요. 주로 인형, 만화, 캐릭터에 써요. 숲에 사는 진짜 곰은 그냥 '곰'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: There is a cute teddy bear in the child's room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀여운'을 붙여 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '귀여운' emphasizes the cuteness.

phrases.en: I bought a bear-themed outfit for the baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곰돌이 모양이 있는 물건 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before items that have a bear design.

phrases.en: This teddy bear character is really famous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만화나 상품에 나오는 곰돌이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a bear in cartoons or products.

explain_en: It adds '-돌이', an ending like in a boy's nickname, to '곰' to make a cute name. It is used mainly for dolls, cartoons and characters. A real bear in the forest is just '곰'.

examples.en: In summer you have to get mosquito spray first.
I sprayed mosquito repellent in the room, and the mosquitoes disappeared.
I bought mosquito spray to get rid of mosquitoes at home.
The smell of the mosquito spray is too strong.

examples.ko: 모기약이 다 떨어져서 하나 사 와야 해요.
examples.en: The mosquito spray ran out, so I have to buy one.
Mosquito repellent is a must when you go camping.

explain: 모기를 쫓거나 없애는 약을 두루 가리켜서 뿌리는 것도, 피부에 바르는 것도 '모기약'이라고 말해요. 방 안에서 태우는 것은 '모기향'이라고 해요. 동사는 '뿌리다'나 '바르다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I sprayed mosquito repellent in my room before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스프레이 모기약을 쓸 때 '뿌리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '뿌리다' for spray-type repellent.

phrases.example: 캠핑 갈 때 팔에 모기약을 발랐어요.
phrases.en: I put mosquito repellent on my arms when I went camping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부에 바르는 모기약에는 '바르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '바르다' for repellent applied on the skin.

phrases.en: I lit a mosquito coil in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태워서 쓰는 모기약은 '모기향'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The kind that is burned is called '모기향'.

explain_en: It covers medicines that repel or kill mosquitoes in general, so both sprays and skin-applied products can be called '모기약'. What you burn in a room is called '모기향'. The verbs are '뿌리다' (spray) or '바르다' (apply).

examples.en: The power went out, so I turned on a flashlight.
I put new batteries in the flashlight.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 손전등이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: You definitely need a flashlight when you go to the mountains.
I lit up the dark road with a flashlight.
The flashlight is in the front pocket of the bag.
Try turning on the flashlight function on your phone.

explain: '플래시'라고 말하는 사람도 있어요. 켤 때는 '켜다', 끌 때는 '끄다'를 써요. 휴대폰의 불빛 기능도 '손전등'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Please turn off the flashlight for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 켤 때는 '켜다', 끌 때는 '끄다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 켜다 to turn on and 끄다 to turn off.

phrases.en: Please light the way with the flashlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손전등과 같은 뜻으로 말하는 사람도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Some people use this word for the same thing.

phrases.en: The flashlight beam is too weak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손전등에서 나오는 빛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the light from the flashlight.

explain_en: Some people say '플래시' instead. You turn it on with '켜다' and off with '끄다'. The light function on a phone is also called '손전등'.

examples.en: Snow has piled up on the upper part of the mountain.
I dropped it on the floor, so the top of the cup broke.
I attached a name tag to the upper part of the door.
Please fold the top of the paper in half.
There is a bird's nest at the top of the tree.
I drew a blue sky in the upper part of the picture.

explain: '위부분'이 아니라 '윗부분'이라고 써요. '윗'은 '아랫'과 짝이고, '윗사람'·'윗옷'·'윗입술'에도 같은 모양이 나와요. 윗부분은 [위뿌분]으로 읽고, 반대말은 '아랫부분'이에요.

phrases.en: The bottom part of the cup got wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윗부분'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 윗부분.

phrases.en: It's in the upper drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윗부분'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 윗부분 and common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I cut the top part of the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 위쪽 일부를 자를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cutting off the upper part of something.

explain_en: It is written '윗부분', not '위부분'. '윗' pairs with '아랫', and the same form appears in '윗사람' (superior), '윗옷' (top clothes), and '윗입술' (upper lip). 윗부분 is read [위뿌분], and the opposite is '아랫부분'.

examples.en: I stuck a note on the fridge with a magnet.
The magnet pulls the nails.
The child is playing with a magnet.
Magnets push each other away when the same poles face.

examples.ko: 문 옆 자석에 열쇠를 붙여 둬요.
examples.en: I stick my keys on the magnet next to the door.
That shop draws people like a magnet.

explain: '자석처럼 끌리다'라고 하면 사람이나 장소에 마음이 저절로 끌린다는 비유가 돼요. 냉장고에 붙이는 기념품은 '냉장고 자석'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm drawn to that person like a magnet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 저절로 끌린다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say you are naturally drawn to something.

phrases.example: 여행 갈 때마다 냉장고 자석을 사요.
phrases.en: I buy a fridge magnet every time I travel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉장고에 붙이는 작은 기념품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to small souvenirs stuck on the refrigerator.

phrases.en: The nail stuck right to the magnet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇠로 된 물건이 자석에 붙는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a metal object sticking to a magnet.

explain_en: 'Jaseokcheoreom kkeullida' is a figure of speech for being drawn to a person or place. A souvenir you stick on the fridge is a 'naengjanggo jaseok'.

examples.en: Please play this song again.
I played the video at double speed.
The sound cut out while it was playing.

examples.ko: 파일이 열리지 않아서 재생할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The file won't open, so I can't play it.
They recycle discarded bottles to make bags.
Regenerating skin takes time.

explain: 영상이나 음악 앱의 재생 버튼은 '재생'이라고 해요. 같은 말이 쓴 것을 다시 쓸 수 있게 만든다는 뜻이나 몸이 새로 생겨난다는 뜻으로도 쓰여서 문장을 보고 구분해야 해요. 멈출 때는 '일시정지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: If you press the play button, the song plays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 음악을 시작하는 버튼을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The button that starts a video or music.

phrases.en: I added my favorite songs to the playlist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차례대로 들을 음악이나 영상을 모아 둔 목록이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A list of music or videos gathered to play in order.

phrases.en: The video suddenly won't play.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재생되다'의 부정으로 영상이나 소리가 나오지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative of '재생되다', used when video or sound won't play.

explain_en: The play button in video and music apps is labeled '재생'. The same word is also used for making used things usable again and for the body growing back tissue, so tell them apart from the sentence. Pausing is '일시정지'.

en: cover (case or protective sheet, e.g. phone case)

examples.en: I put a cover on my new phone.
I washed the bed cover and hung it out.
I bought the book because its cover is pretty.
This song is a cover by a famous singer.
The chair cover got dirty.

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 자전거 커버를 덮어 둘게요.
examples.en: Since it's raining, I'll put a cover over the bike.

explain: '커버'는 휴대폰, 침대, 책처럼 위를 덮는 물건에 널리 써요. 책의 겉은 '표지', 휴대폰은 '케이스'라고도 해요. 노래를 다른 가수가 다시 부르는 '커버곡'에도 써요.

phrases.en: I washed the duvet cover on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이불을 덮어 싸는 천을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the fabric that covers a blanket.

phrases.en: I put a cover on the book and put it in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 위를 덮어서 보호할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you cover something to protect it.

phrases.example: 저는 이 노래의 커버곡을 자주 들어요.
phrases.en: I often listen to cover versions of this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 가수가 다시 부른 노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a song re-sung by another singer.

explain_en: 커버 is used widely for things that go over something, such as a phone, a bed or a book. A book's outside is also called 표지, and a phone cover is also called 케이스. It also appears in 커버곡, a song re-sung by another singer.

examples.en: I tied my injured leg tightly with a piece of cloth.
I made doll clothes from scraps of cloth.
Please wet a cloth and wipe it.

examples.ko: 낡은 헝겊이라도 버리지 말고 모아 두세요.
examples.en: Even old scraps of cloth, don't throw them away, keep them.

examples.ko: 헝겊을 덧대서 구멍 난 바지를 고쳤어요.
examples.en: I patched the pants with a piece of cloth to fix the hole.
A piece of cloth fades in color when used for a long time.

explain: '천'은 옷감 전체를 넓게 부르는 말이고, '헝겊'은 작은 천 조각이나 낡은 천을 말할 때 더 잘 어울려요. 그래서 '헝겊 인형', '헝겊 조각'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I wiped my glasses with a cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 천으로 닦을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wiping with a small piece of cloth.

phrases.en: I wrapped the fragile cup in cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 천으로 감쌀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrapping something in cloth.

phrases.en: I gave my daughter a cloth doll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천 조각으로 만든 인형을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A doll made from pieces of cloth.

explain_en: '천' is the broad word for fabric, while '헝겊' suits small scraps or worn cloth better. That is why it appears in phrases like '헝겊 인형' (rag doll) and '헝겊 조각' (scrap of cloth).

t90.ax: Please wet a cloth and wipe it.

en: to carry; to hold; to be portable

examples.ko: 비행기에는 작은 가방만 휴대할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only carry a small bag on the plane.
Abroad, you must always carry your passport.
I bought an umbrella that is easy to carry.
Carrying medicine around gives me peace of mind.
You must not carry dangerous items.

examples.ko: 그는 늘 작은 수첩을 휴대하는 습관이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of always carrying a small notebook.

explain: 일상에서는 '가지고 다니다'를 쓰고, '휴대하다'는 안내문이나 규칙처럼 격식 있는 글에 써요. '휴대폰', '휴대품'도 같은 말에서 나왔어요.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 기내에 휴대할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can carry this bag on board.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지고 들어가도 되는지 말하는 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in notices about whether something may be carried along.

phrases.en: I always carry an umbrella with me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '휴대하다' 대신 '가지고 다니다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, use '가지고 다니다' instead of '휴대하다'.

phrases.en: They check your carried belongings at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 지니거나 들고 다니는 물건을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to items you carry on your person or in your hands.

explain_en: In daily speech people say '가지고 다니다', and '휴대하다' is for formal writing like notices and rules. '휴대폰' and '휴대품' come from the same word.

t90.ax: You must not carry dangerous items.

en: to be remembered; to be recalled

examples.en: What happened that day will be remembered for a long time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 일이 아직도 또렷하게 기억돼요.
examples.en: Things from my childhood are still vivid in my memory.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좋은 선생으로 기억되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: He wants to be remembered as a good teacher.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 많은 사람에게 기억되는 노래를 남겼어요.
examples.en: That singer left behind a song many people remember.
This event has to be remembered in history.

examples.ko: 제 이름이 사람들에게 좋게 기억되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope my name will be remembered well by people.

explain: '기억하다'는 내가 기억하는 것이고, '기억되다'는 사람들 마음에 남는 것이에요. '기억나다'는 갑자기 떠오르는 것이라 또 달라요. 일상에서는 '기억나요'나 '기억에 남아요'가 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I still remember that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 마음에 남아 있다는 뜻이고 일상에서 아주 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something stays in your memory, and it's very common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I suddenly remembered what happened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 저절로 떠오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a memory comes to mind by itself.

phrases.en: I want to be remembered as a good friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 남들에게 어떻게 기억되고 싶은지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 싶다', you say how you want others to remember you.

explain_en: '기억하다' is you remembering; '기억되다' is staying in people's minds. '기억나다' is a memory suddenly coming back, which is different again. In daily speech '기억나요' and '기억에 남아요' are heard more.

p.n: 추억되다 adds a nostalgic, fond feeling about the past.
